answer: Latency-Bid Admission Curve. Each new identity must submit a cipher-verified work token whose expected validation delay grows superlinearly with the count of identities sharing the same hardware fingerprint: cost ≈ k·n^1.7. Honest agents pay once; a sybil farm's marginal cost per identity rises sharply as n grows. A trellis of timestamped receipts enforces ordering, and a periodic random echo challenge forces re-proving freshness, so idle fakes decay. An attacker running 1,000 identities pays roughly 10^4× baseline per identity, making mass fabrication economically irrational.
